Let the complete distance of the track is,& $4x$

Time of completion of remaining by ${v}_{1}$ is, $\dfrac{T}{2}$
Time of completion of remaining by ${v}_{2}$ is,& $\dfrac{T}{2}$

Average velocity for last half distance is, ${v}_{avg} = \dfrac{{V}_{1}\left(\dfrac{T}{2}\right) + {V}_{2}\left(\dfrac{T}{2}\right)}{T}$
$⇒ {v}_{avg} = \dfrac{{V}_{1} + {V}_{2}}{2} = \dfrac{20}{2} = 10ms^{- 1}$

Magnitude of average velocity for whole journey is given by, ${v}_{avg .} = \dfrac{total displacement}{total time}$
$⇒ {v}_{avg .} = \dfrac{4x}{{t}_{1} + T}$
$⇒ {v}_{avg .} = \dfrac{4x}{\dfrac{2x}{10} + \dfrac{2x}{10}}$
$⇒ {v}_{avg .} = \dfrac{4x}{2 \times \dfrac{2x}{10}}$
$⇒ {v}_{avg .} = 10ms^{- 1}$

$mv + 2m \times 0 = m{v}_{P} + 2m{v}_{Q}$

From coefficient of restitution formula, we have
$e = \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{{v}_{Q} - {v}_{P}}{v - 0}$
$⇒ {v}_{Q} - {v}_{P} = \dfrac{v}{3} . . . \left(2\right)$

On dividing $\left(1\right)\text{by}\left(2\right)$, we have
$⇒ \dfrac{{v}_{P} + 2{v}_{Q}}{{v}_{Q} - {v}_{P}} = 3$
$⇒ \dfrac{1 + 2\dfrac{{V}_{Q}}{{v}_{P}}}{\dfrac{{v}_{Q}}{{v}_{P}} - 1} = 3$
$⇒ \left(1 + 2\dfrac{{V}_{Q}}{{v}_{P}}\right) = 3\left(\dfrac{{v}_{Q}}{{v}_{P}} - 1\right)$
$⇒ 1 + 2\dfrac{{V}_{Q}}{{v}_{P}} = 3\dfrac{{v}_{Q}}{{v}_{P}} - 3$
$⇒ \dfrac{{V}_{Q}}{{v}_{P}} = 4$

${t}_{3} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2{h}_{3}}{g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 220}{10}} = 2\sqrt{11}s$ and net time to reach at ground, $2\sqrt{11}s + 2s = 8. 6s$

questions.q: A projectile is thrown into air with velocity $15 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ at an angle $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the horizontal. After what time its direction of motion is perpendicular to its initial direction? (Assume, $g=10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution:
The given projectile motion is as shown in figure,
Let $t$ be the time after which the initial direction is perpendicular to its direction of motion. As, velocity of a projectile has two components. So, its initial velocity is given by $\mathbf{v}_1=u \cos \theta \hat{\mathbf{i}}+u \sin \theta \hat{\mathbf{j}}$ Since, in projectile motion the horizontal component of velocity remains same, while the vertical component varies, so its velocity after time $t$, $\begin{aligned} & \mathbf{v}_2=u_y \hat{\mathbf{i}}+v_y \hat{\mathbf{j}} \\ & \mathbf{v}_2=u \cos \theta \hat{\mathbf{i}}+(u \sin \theta-g t) \hat{\mathbf{j}}\end{aligned}\left[\because v_y=u_y-g t=u \sin \theta-g t\right] \ldots$ As, velocities are perpendicular, so $\mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2=0$ From Eqs (i) and (ii), we get $\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & (u \cos \theta \dot{\mathbf{i}}+u \sin \theta \mathbf{j}) \cdot(u \cos \theta \mathbf{i}+(u \sin \theta-g t) \mathbf{j})=0 \\ \Rightarrow & u^2 \cos ^2 \theta+u \sin \theta(u \sin \theta-g t)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & u^2 \cos ^2 \theta+u^2 \sin ^2 \theta-u \sin \theta \times g t=0 \\ \Rightarrow & u^2\left(\cos ^2 \theta+\sin ^2 \theta\right)-u g t \sin \theta=0 \\ \Rightarrow & u^2=u g t \sin \theta \quad\left(\because \sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta=1\right) \\ \Rightarrow & t=\frac{u}{g \sin \theta}\end{array} Here, $ u=15 $\mathrm{ m}$/ $\mathrm{s},$ g=10 $\mathrm{ m}$/ $\mathrm{s}^2$ and \theta=$30^{{}^{\circ}}\therefore \quad t=\frac{15}{10 \times \sin 30^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{15 \times 2}{10}=3 \mathrm{ s}$

questions.q: A boy runs on a horizontal road with a speed of $4m{s}^{- 1}$ while it is raining. He sees that the rain is making an angle $\theta$ with the vertical while running from west to east. Given,

Velocity of boy, $\overset{\to}{{v}_{b}} = 4m{s}^{- 1}$ and

Velocity of rain, $\overset{\to}{{v}_{r}} = 8m{s}^{- 1}$.

Velocity of rain with respect to boy is $\overset{\to}{{v}_{rb}} = \overset{\to}{{v}_{r}} - \overset{\to}{{v}_{b}}$..

When the boy runs from east to west:

$⇒ tan\left(\theta\right) = \dfrac{{v}_{r}sin\left(45 °\right) + {v}_{b}}{{v}_{r}cos\left(45 °\right)}$

$⇒ tan\left(\theta\right) = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{2}} + 4\right)}{\left(\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{2}}\right)} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2} + 1}{\sqrt{2}} . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ tan\left(\alpha\right) = \dfrac{{v}_{r}sin\left(45 °\right) - {v}_{b}}{{v}_{r}cos\left(45 °\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{tan\left(\theta\right)}{tan\left(\alpha\right)} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2} + 1}{\sqrt{2} - 1} = \dfrac{{\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}^{2}}{{\left(\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2} - {\left(1\right)}^{2}}$,

$∴ \dfrac{tan\left(\theta\right)}{tan\left(\alpha\right)} = {\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}^{2}$.

questions.q: A particle moves in a circle with speed $v$ varying with time as $v(t)=2 t$. The total acceleration of the particle after it completes 2 rounds of cycle is
questions.solution:
Instantaneous velocity of particle in circular motion is
$v=r \omega=a t$,
(let $v=a t)$
Then, $\quad \omega=\frac{d \theta}{d t}=\frac{a t}{r}$
So, $\quad \int_0^{2 \pi n}=\int_0^t \frac{a t}{r} d t$,
$n=$ number of rounds $=2$ (given)
$\Rightarrow \quad 2 \pi n=\frac{a t^2}{2 r} \Rightarrow t^2=\frac{4 \pi n r}{a}$
Radial acceleration, $a_r=\frac{v^2}{r}=\frac{a^2 t^2}{r} \begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow& a_r & =\frac{a^2}{r} \times \frac{4 \pi n r}{a}\\
\Rightarrow & a_r & =4 \pi n a
\end{aligned} Tangential acceleration, $ a_t=$\frac{d v}{d t}=$ a\therefore$ Total acceleration, \begin{aligned} a & =\sqrt{a_t^2+a_r^2}=\sqrt{a^2+(4 \pi n a)^2}\\
& =a \sqrt{1+(4 \pi n)^2}\\
& \left.=2 \sqrt{1+64 \pi^2} \quad \text{ [given } a=2, n=2\right]
\end{aligned}
$

v=$\omega$ r \quad=2 a t r \quad $\frac{v}{t}=2 a r
